lifecycles._note: Light read-only lifecycle: covers all collection GETs that 2xx with no resource. Five endpoints confirmed live 2026-06-29: GET /v1/loadbalancers (listloadbalancers) 200, GET /v1/lb-health-checks (listlbhealthchecks) 200, GET /v1/lb-listeners (listlblisteners) 200, GET /v1/lb-server-groups (listlbservergroups) 200, GET /v1/loadbalancers/certificates (listloadbalancercertificates) 200. The id-bound GETs (showloadbalancer, showlbhealthcheck, showlblistener, showlbservergroup, showlbservergroupmember, showloadbalancercertificate, showloadbalancerpublicnatip, showloadbalancerprivatenatip) and GET /v1/lb-server-groups/{id}/members (listlbservergroupmembers) all need real ids (ledger: 0 LBs in account). This lifecycle deliberately targets only the safely reachable collection endpoints. No teardown required (read-only). Ceiling for this lifecycle: 5/34. All write ops + id-bound GETs remain in the heavy lifecycle (gen-heavy-lb-members, generated__wave5-net.json — members-nat 은 2026-07-08 DEDUP §C 로 은퇴). Note: ledger shows 6/34 already covered (5 smoke GETs + showlbhealthcheck from system HCs); this lifecycle re-anchors those 5 collection GETs explicitly.

lifecycles._note: Loadbalancer server-group MEMBERS + static-NAT write coverage (Wave 2, NOT runtime-proven, HEAVY/billable). The 8 uncovered LB writes all hang off a real loadbalancer / lb-server-group, so this lifecycle stands up a minimal LB stack under the session-shared VPC (adopt:vpc — does NOT self-create a VPC) and creates its OWN subnet under it (the heavy lifecycles share the VPC but each make their own subnet, per vpc-scheduling-strategy.md): subnet -> LB-HEALTH-CHECK FIRST -> lb -> lb-server-group (bodies mirror the proven heavy-shared-networking LB chain). ORDERING FIX (userguide lb-health-check-before-server-group, run 27306490231 LbHealthCheckNotFoundError): the server-group create selects a health check from the PRE-CREATED list, so lb-healthcheck-create now runs BEFORE lb-create/lb-server-group — the HC gets the whole LB provisioning window to settle before the server group references {lb_health_check_id}. Other userguide facts (networking__loadbalancer.yaml, 2026-06-11, pending live validation): LB name 3-63 [A-Za-z0-9-_] (regrlb{ualpha} complies); one LB consumes 4 IPs of its service subnet (service+SNAT+2 HC — our own 10.138.5.0/24 fallback subnet has room; service_ip 10.124.0.30 only resolves when the shared subnet is adopted, per fixed_ip_map); SNAT/HC IPs are immutable post-create; attaching a Public NAT IP requires an IGW on the VPC — static-nat-create sends an empty publicip_id on an IGW-less VPC and stays 4xx-tolerant by design. Then it exercises members (add -> set -> remove-single -> remove-bulk) and static-nats (public static-nat create/delete on the loadbalancer, private static-nat create/delete). MEMBERS family: addlbservergroupmembers POST returns $.members[0].id (soft-captured into member_id from response_example); set/remove-single reference {member_id}; remove-bulk uses {member_id_list:[{member_id}]}. member_ip is an arbitrary in-subnet IP — no backend VM required to register a member. STATIC-NAT family: createloadbalancerpublicnatip needs a real publicip_id and createloadbalancerprivatenatip needs private_nat_id+private_nat_ip_id — we have none, so those POSTs send empty-string ids, are OPTIONAL and 4xx-tolerant; the static_nat create returns $.static_nat.id (soft-captured) so the matching DELETE reuses it, else sends {static_nat_id} literal which still norm-matches the catalog '*' and records coverage. All families are isolated optional groups so one bad body skips only its family (cleaned up children-first). layer_type:L4 + LB enum guesses inherit the heavy-shared-networking UNVALIDATED caveat. Covers all 8 LB WRITE ops: POST/DELETE /v1/lb-server-groups/{id}/members, PUT/DELETE /v1/lb-server-groups/{id}/members/{member_id}, POST/DELETE /v1/loadbalancers/{id}/static-nats, POST/DELETE /v1/loadbalancers/{id}/private-static-nats.

steps.name: lb-healthcheck-create
steps._note: REPAIR 2026-07-06 (HB4 400 SubnetNotAssociatedWithLoadBalancer, run 28738115294, OFFLINE repair — see CAMPAIGN-C3-100-repair-log.md #HB4b): live error was 'Unable to process the request because the chosen subnet does not contain a Load Balancer ... Please ensure a Load Balancer exists within the subnet before attempting again' for THIS SAME {subnet_id} (own subnet, not a mismatched reference — both lb-create and lb-healthcheck-create already read the identical {subnet_id} captured by this lifecycle's own create-subnet step). Root cause was ORDERING, not a wrong subnet reference: the prior 2026-06-xx fix moved lb-healthcheck-create BEFORE lb-create so lb-servergroup-create could select a PRE-CREATED health check (avoiding LbHealthCheckNotFoundError) — but that made lb-healthcheck-create run before any LB existed in the subnet, which the health-check API requires. Fix: lb-create + lb-wait now run FIRST (LB lands in {subnet_id}), THEN lb-healthcheck-create (subnet now has an LB), THEN lb-servergroup-create (health check already exists) — satisfies both constraints in one order. UNVERIFIED LIVE (offline repair) — next heavy dispatch must confirm 2xx.

steps.name: list-igw-for-static-nat
steps._note: REPAIR 2026-07-07 (HB4c, run 28833316852, OFFLINE repair — see CAMPAIGN-C3-100-repair-log.md §HB4c item 2): create-igw-for-static-nat 400 `scp-network.internet-gateway.already-associated` ("The VPC(...) is already associated with an Internet Gateway(...)") — CONFIRMED from the observation's own error body: at most ONE IGW per VPC is permitted, and this SAME shared VPC is ALSO targeted by networking__vpn.json's own create-igw-for-vpn in the SAME concurrent run (both adopt the one session-shared VPC, do not self-create) — whichever family's create runs SECOND now 400s. Fix: adopt-or-create — list existing IGWs on `{vpc_id}` first (`networking/vpc/listinternetgateways`, response_example wraps as `internet_gateways[]`); if one already exists (created by the VPN family, or a prior run) capture its id into `igw_id` so wait/set-igw and the static-nat family proceed against a real IGW either way. If none exists yet this finds nothing and the following create-igw-for-static-nat step makes one. See that step's note for why the DELETE step must NOT reuse this adopted `igw_id`.

steps.name: create-igw-for-static-nat

json.description: API regression IGW for LB static-nat

steps._note: REPAIR 2026-07-06 (HB4 400 igw-required-for-static-nat, run 28738115294, OFFLINE repair — see CAMPAIGN-C3-100-repair-log.md #HB4b): static-nat-create failed 'Cannot create Public NAT: No Internet Gateway (IGW) found in the VPC'. Pattern lifted verbatim from the proven networking__vpc.json create-internet-gateway-for-nat fix (CONFIRMED live 2026-06-23: nat-gateway also requires an attached IGW) — create IGW on the same VPC, wait ACTIVE, PUT/set it (the set call is what the NAT-gateway precedent found necessary to mark the VPC's IGW as attached/active before the NAT-family create), THEN attempt static-nat-create. Grouped+optional (staticnat) so a shared-VPC IGW collision with another concurrent adopter (409/quota) only skips this NAT family, not the whole LB lifecycle; teardown deletes the IGW after static-nat-delete, before the VPC/subnet teardown. UPDATE 2026-07-07 (HB4c): this WAS observed as a genuine collision in run 28833316852 (400 already-associated, VPN family created the IGW first) — added the list-igw-for-static-nat adopt-or-create bootstrap above, so this 400 (this family running second) is now a non-event. `owned_igw_id` is captured ONLY here (from OUR OWN create response), separately from the adoption-tolerant `igw_id`, so the cleanup dict above and the explicit `delete-igw-for-static-nat` teardown step below key off `owned_igw_id` — if this create 400s (adopted, not owned), `owned_igw_id` stays unset and both those DELETE calls hit an unresolved literal path (safe 404), NEVER the VPN family's real IGW. UNVERIFIED LIVE (offline repair) — next heavy dispatch must confirm 2xx AND that a concurrent run with networking-vpn-gateway-tunnel no longer 400s on either side's create.

steps.name: create-publicip-for-static-nat

json.description: API regression public IP for LB static-nat

steps._note: REPAIR 2026-07-07 (HB4b-2, run 28827996068, OFFLINE repair — see CAMPAIGN-C3-100-repair-log.md #HB4b-2 item 4): static-nat-create 404s `scp-loadbalancer.loadbalancers.PublicIpNotFound` ("Public IP '' is not found") even AFTER the HB4b IGW fix — CONFIRMED from the observation: the body sent `publicip_id:""` BY DESIGN (see this lifecycle's top-level _note, written when there was no real publicip_id available), and `data/api_docs.json` models['networking/loadbalancer/staticnatcreaterequestdetail'] confirms `publicip_id` is the ONLY field and is required:true — so an empty string was always going to 404, independent of IGW timing (the IGW fix was still necessary — it's a separate precondition — but not sufficient on its own). Fix: create a real public IP (pattern lifted verbatim from networking__vpc.json's proven create-publicip-for-nat / create-publicip-for-vip, both `type:IGW` -> `$.publicip.id`), feed its id into static-nat-create. Own capture name (`static_nat_publicip_id`) to avoid clashing with lb-create's own (intentionally empty) `publicip_id` field elsewhere in this file. Grouped+optional (staticnat) — a quota-limited publicip create only skips this NAT family. Teardown deletes the public IP after static-nat-delete (children-first, alongside delete-igw-for-static-nat). UNVERIFIED LIVE (offline repair) — next heavy dispatch must confirm 2xx.

steps.name: wait-static-nat-active
steps._note: REPAIR 2026-07-07 (HB4d, run 28835929967, OFFLINE repair — see CAMPAIGN-C3-100-repair-log.md §HB4d item 2): static-nat-create (201) was immediately followed by static-nat-delete 400 `scp-loadbalancer.loadbalancers.StaticNatNotDeletableState` ("The static NAT is not in a deletable state (id: ..., state: CREATING)") — the orchestrator had to manually unwind this (GET static-nats -> confirm ACTIVE -> DELETE) because the leftover CREATING NAT then blocked lb-delete (409 associated) which in turn stranded the publicip (ATTACHED) and the shared VPC. UNVERIFIED LIVE (offline repair) — next heavy dispatch must confirm static-nat-delete clears without the 400/409/stranding cascade.

steps.name: static-nat-delete
steps._note: REPAIR 2026-07-07 (HB4d, run 28835929967, OFFLINE repair — see CAMPAIGN-C3-100-repair-log.md §HB4d item 2): belt-and-suspenders alongside the new wait-static-nat-active settle-poll above — retry on 400 (StaticNatNotDeletableState) so a still-CREATING NAT (e.g. poll gave up early, or state flaps) doesn't strand this NAT/publicip/lb/VPC chain a second time.

steps.name: delete-publicip-for-static-nat
steps._note: Delete the public IP created for static-nat-create, children-first (after static-nat-delete releases it, before delete-igw-for-static-nat/delete-subnet/delete-vpc).

steps.name: delete-igw-for-static-nat
steps._note: REPAIR 2026-07-07 (HB4c, run 28833316852, OFFLINE repair — see CAMPAIGN-C3-100-repair-log.md §HB4c item 2): path changed from `{igw_id}` to `{owned_igw_id}` — `igw_id` may now be an ADOPTED IGW (see list-igw-for-static-nat's note) belonging to a concurrently-running lifecycle (e.g. networking__vpn.json's VPN gateway family), and this suite must never delete another family's live resource. `owned_igw_id` is captured only by create-igw-for-static-nat's own 2xx and stays unset when we adopted instead of created, so an adopted case leaves this DELETE targeting an unresolved literal path (safe 404, matches this codebase's established soft-capture-miss convention) instead of the foreign IGW. Delete the IGW created for static-nat-create, children-first (after static-nat-delete, before delete-subnet/delete-vpc). Retry 400 to ride out the not-deletable-state transition (same quirk CONFIRMED for this endpoint in networking__vpc.json).

steps.name: list-lb-certificates
steps._note: Collection read (listloadbalancercertificates) used to source an id for the id-bound show below. networking/loadbalancer has NO certificate CREATE endpoint — LB certificates are minted by security/certificatemanager and only listed/shown here — so the ONLY honest capture source for lb_certificate_id is this list. Soft-captures $.certificates[0].id: if the shared account already has an LB certificate the show becomes a REAL read; otherwise the soft-capture finds nothing and the show fires against the {lb_certificate_id} placeholder (normalizes to the catalog '*' key) and 4xx's, still recording coverage. Tolerant [200,400,403,404].

steps.name: show-lb-certificate
steps._note: id-bound read (showloadbalancercertificate). Closes the lb_certificate_id getid GET /v1/loadbalancers/certificates/{lb_certificate_id} — the service's only remaining static gap. Keys off lb_certificate_id soft-captured from list-lb-certificates (no LB-side create exists for it). Tolerant [200,400,403,404]: a real 2xx needs a pre-existing certificatemanager-issued LB cert on the shared account; absent that the id stays a placeholder and 4xx's, which still records the endpoint as reached.

steps.name: lb-listener-create
steps._note: createlblistener: requires loadbalancer_id + routing_action enum (LB_SERVER_GROUP|URL_REDIRECT). service_port is integer (1-65534). server_group_id is optional. Captures listener_id for probe_reads -> showlblistener catalog coverage. Protocol enum: TCP|UDP|HTTP|HTTPS|TLS|TCP_PROXY. name pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9-_]* 3-63 chars.

steps.name: probe-lb-reads
steps._note: probe_reads records all id-bound GETs under their catalog keys (required for coverage counting). listener_id from lb-listener-create covers showlblistener. lb_certificate_id from list-lb-certificates covers showloadbalancercertificate (2xx only if account has a cert registered via certificatemanager; otherwise 4xx=soft). member_id from members-add covers showlbservergroupmember.
